Hi Alicia — thanks for the context and the export, that helps. Quick summary and two recommended paths we typically use for this scenario: 

Option A — Immediate top-up (pro-rata invoice)
- We add the extra capacity immediately and generate a one-time invoice for the pro-rated amount covering the remainder of your current term.
- Standard uplift rate applies (no additional term commitment).
- Fastest to implement; billing reflects actual months remaining.

Option B — Annualize and blend (preferred if you want smoothing)
- You commit to annualizing the increased capacity for the remainder of your term (we compute the incremental annual spend and divide it across remaining invoices).
- We can apply a blended uplift discount (example: 10% on incremental capacity) if you commit to keep the higher capacity until the next renewal.
- We can also apply a one-time operational credit (we typically handle this as a voucher against the next invoice) up to a modest amount to offset migration work.

What I'll do: Marissa will put together a short stepwise quote (both paths) with precise $ numbers and a draft amendment you can take to procurement. Tessa will confirm the invoicing schedule for each option. If procurement has a PO template or a target approval date, loop that in so we can align timelines.

Attaching: proposal-v1.pdf (workshop-level estimates)

Next steps: Marissa will share the formal quote by EOD tomorrow. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you want to walk numbers.
